ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, a regular octagon is assembled with four quadrilaterals as depicted in Figure 1 and four diamonds as illustrated in Figure 2 (as in Figure 3). What is the ratio of the area of the shaded part to the area of the blank part in Figure 3?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw $BE\perp AD$ at E through the vertex B of the rhombus; Let the center of the regular octagon be point O, with one side being MN. Connect OM and ON, and draw $MP\perp ON$ at P through point M. Suppose the side length of the regular octagon is $a$, then we have $AB=AD=MN=a$,\\
$\therefore \angle ABC=180^\circ-360^\circ\div 8=135^\circ$, $\angle MON=360^\circ\div 8=45^\circ$,\\
$\because AD\parallel BC$,\\
$\therefore \angle BAE=180^\circ-\angle ABC=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore BE=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}AB=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}a$,\\
$\therefore S_{\text{rhombus}ABCD}=AD\cdot BE=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}a^{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ the area of the blank part $=4\times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}a^{2}=2\sqrt{2}a^{2}$,\\
$\because \angle MON=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore OP=PM$, let $OP=PM=b$, then $OM=ON=\sqrt{2}b$,\\
$\therefore PN=(\sqrt{2}-1)b$,\\
In $\triangle MPN$, $PM^{2}+PN^{2}=MN^{2}$,\\
$\therefore b^{2}+(\sqrt{2}-1)^{2}b^{2}=a^{2}$,\\
Upon rearranging: $b^{2}=\frac{2+\sqrt{2}}{4}a^{2}$,\\
$\therefore S_{\triangle OMN}=\frac{1}{2}ON\cdot PM=\frac{1}{2}\times \sqrt{2}b\cdot b=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}b^{2}=\frac{1+\sqrt{2}}{4}a^{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ the area of the regular octagon is: $8\times \frac{1+\sqrt{2}}{4}a^{2}=2(1+\sqrt{2})a^{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ the area of the shaded part is: $2(1+\sqrt{2})a^{2}-2\sqrt{2}a^{2}=2a^{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ the ratio of the area of the shaded part to the area of the blank part $=\frac{2a^{2}}{2\sqrt{2}a^{2}}=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}}$.

First read the image: Figure 3 is a regular octagon with a gray central four-point shaded region and four unshaded diamond/rhombus regions around it; each unshaded diamond uses two adjacent sides of the regular octagon, so its side length equals the octagon side length. method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中有三个图形。图1是一个灰色四边形拼块，图2是一个空白菱形拼块，图3是一个正八边形，由中央灰色四尖形区域和周围四个空白菱形区域拼成。图3中每个空白菱形都贴着正八边形的两条相邻边，因此这些菱形的边长与正八边形边长相同。

推理：设正八边形的边长为 a。正八边形的内角为 135°，所以每个空白菱形的两条相邻边长为 a，夹角为 135°。因此一个空白菱形的面积为 a^2 sin135° = (√2/2)a^2。四个空白菱形总面积为 4 × (√2/2)a^2 = 2√2 a^2。

正八边形边长为 a 时，总面积为 2(1+√2)a^2。灰色阴影部分面积等于正八边形面积减去空白部分面积：2(1+√2)a^2 - 2√2 a^2 = 2a^2。

所以阴影部分面积与空白部分面积之比为 2a^2 : 2√2 a^2 = 1 : √2 = √2/2。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, a regular octagon is assembled with four quadrilaterals as depicted in Figure 1 and four diamonds as illustrated in Figure 2 (as in Figure 3). What is the ratio of the area of the shaded part to the area of the blank part in Figure 3?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw $BE\perp AD$ at E through the vertex B of the rhombus; Let the center of the regular octagon be point O, with one side being MN. Connect OM and ON, and draw $MP\perp ON$ at P through point M. Suppose the side length of the regular octagon is $a$, then we have $AB=AD=MN=a$,\\
$\therefore \angle ABC=180^\circ-360^\circ\div 8=135^\circ$, $\angle MON=360^\circ\div 8=45^\circ$,\\
$\because AD\parallel BC$,\\
$\therefore \angle BAE=180^\circ-\angle ABC=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore BE=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}AB=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}a$,\\
$\therefore S_{\text{rhombus}ABCD}=AD\cdot BE=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}a^{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ the area of the blank part $=4\times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}a^{2}=2\sqrt{2}a^{2}$,\\
$\because \angle MON=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore OP=PM$, let $OP=PM=b$, then $OM=ON=\sqrt{2}b$,\\
$\therefore PN=(\sqrt{2}-1)b$,\\
In $\triangle MPN$, $PM^{2}+PN^{2}=MN^{2}$,\\
$\therefore b^{2}+(\sqrt{2}-1)^{2}b^{2}=a^{2}$,\\
Upon rearranging: $b^{2}=\frac{2+\sqrt{2}}{4}a^{2}$,\\
$\therefore S_{\triangle OMN}=\frac{1}{2}ON\cdot PM=\frac{1}{2}\times \sqrt{2}b\cdot b=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}b^{2}=\frac{1+\sqrt{2}}{4}a^{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ the area of the regular octagon is: $8\times \frac{1+\sqrt{2}}{4}a^{2}=2(1+\sqrt{2})a^{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ the area of the shaded part is: $2(1+\sqrt{2})a^{2}-2\sqrt{2}a^{2}=2a^{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ the ratio of the area of the shaded part to the area of the blank part $=\frac{2a^{2}}{2\sqrt{2}a^{2}}=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw $BE\perp AD$ at E through the vertex B of the rhombus; Let the center of the regular octagon be point O, with one side being MN. Connect OM and ON, and draw $MP\perp ON$ at P through point M. Suppose the side length of the regular octagon is $a$, then we have $AB=AD=MN=a$,\\ $\therefore \angle ABC=180^\circ-360^\circ\div 8=135^\circ$, $\angle MON=360^\circ\div 8=45^\circ$,\\ $\because AD\parallel BC$,\\ $\therefore \angle BAE=180^\circ-\angle ABC=45^\circ$,\\ $\therefore BE=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}AB=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}a$,\\ $\therefore S_{\text{rhombus}ABCD}=AD\cdot BE=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}a^{2}$,\\ $\therefore$ the area of the blank part $=4\times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}a^{2}=2\sqrt{2}a^{2}$,\\ $\because \angle MON=45^\circ$,\\ $\therefore OP=PM$, let $OP=PM=b$, then $OM=ON=\sqrt{2}b$,\\ $\therefore PN=(\sqrt{2}-1)b$,\\ In $\triangle MPN$, $PM^{2}+PN^{2}=MN^{2}$,\\ $\therefore b^{2}+(\sqrt{2}-1)^{2}b^{2}=a^{2}$,\\ Upon rearranging: $b^{2}=\frac{2+\sqrt{2}}{4}a^{2}$,\\ $\therefore S_{\triangle OMN}=\frac{1}{2}ON\cdot PM=\frac{1}{2}\times \sqrt{2}b\cdot b=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}b^{2}=\frac{1+\sqrt{2}}{4}a^{2}$,\\ $\therefore$ the area of the regular octagon is: $8\times \frac{1+\sqrt{2}}{4}a^{2}=2(1+\sqrt{2})a^{2}$,\\ $\therefore$ the area of the shaded part is: $2(1+\sqrt{2})a^{2}-2\sqrt{2}a^{2}=2a^{2}$,\\ $\therefore$ the ratio of the area of the shaded part to the area of the blank part $=\frac{2a^{2}}{2\sqrt{2}a^{2}}=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}}$.
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: There are three figures in the diagram. Figure 1 is a gray quadrilateral puzzle piece, Figure 2 is a blank rhombus puzzle piece, and Figure 3 is a regular octagon, made by assembling a central gray four-pointed region and four surrounding blank rhombus regions. In Figure 3, each blank rhombus is attached to two adjacent sides of the regular octagon, so the side lengths of these rhombuses are the same as the side length of the regular octagon.

Reasoning: Let the side length of the regular octagon be a. The interior angle of a regular octagon is 135°, so the two adjacent side lengths of each blank rhombus are a, and the included angle is 135°. Therefore, the area of one blank rhombus is a^2 sin135° = (√2/2)a^2. The total area of the four blank rhombuses is 4 × (√2/2)a^2 = 2√2 a^2.

When the side length of the regular octagon is a, its total area is 2(1+√2)a^2. The area of the gray shaded part equals the area of the regular octagon minus the area of the blank parts: 2(1+√2)a^2 - 2√2 a^2 = 2a^2.

Therefore, the ratio of the area of the shaded part to the area of the blank parts is 2a^2 : 2√2 a^2 = 1 : √2 = √2/2.
